reason: E1 directly supports the Cr negative stress and SRO premise, but it does not link SRO to secondary phase nucleation or demonstrate the cooling-rate dependence claimed. E2 shows cooling-rate effects on phase formation in a different alloy (CrMnFeCoNiP), not CrCoFeNiAl, and does not address SRO or atomic stress mechanisms, providing only indirect, loosely related support for the diffusion/kinetic premise.
premises: Cr atoms in 3d HEAs exhibit negative atomic stress, while other atoms exhibit positive stress
This stress difference drives chemical short-range order (SRO) formation
SRO development requires sufficient atomic diffusion during cooling
SRO-induced local segregation creates nucleation sites for secondary phases during subsequent annealing
Rapid quenching suppresses diffusion and preserves a homogeneous BCC state
